text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000169 bills 99215 at roughly double the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including simple acute visits, but too few 99215 charts came back to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share holds across every complexity band, including patients with zero or one condition, so a sicker panel does not explain it. The low-complexity sample also shows 99215 billed for brief acute problems such as UTI (C0096163, C0096213, C0096495), rash (C0096299, C0097661), URI (C0096359) and a Z09 follow-up (C0096433), which is a pattern consistent with upcoding. Against that, all three documented 99215 claims (C0096905, C0097596, C0098144) support the billed level, and only one note with moderate-or-higher data reviewed lacked a lab or test line, so there is little sign of cloned notes. The 99214 claims, which dominate this provider's volume, were documented below the billed level at roughly four times the all-provider rate (for example C0097096 and C0097659, both low MDM), but 28 charts is a small sample. A reviewer should first request records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the 0-condition acute visits, and pull a larger 99214 sample to test whether the elevated 99214 mismatch rate holds."}
